definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time

definitions.definition: P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.
For 0<gamma<=1, agamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, agamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and agamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

definitions.type: family of source periodic Sobolev spaces
definitions.definition: For each real s, Hsrc^s is the space of 2*pi-periodic distributions h with 2*pi*sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s*|Fourier(h)(k)|^2 finite, equipped with the square root of that expression as its norm. The Fourier transform is D002, on the same periodic coordinate Ttor, including the zero mode. Equivalently it is the completion of trigonometric polynomials in this unnormalized norm, with negative orders interpreted distributionally. This is the unnormalized Fourier Sobolev convention used in the Li–Wu source estimates.

L2src=Hsrc^0 on the same torus Ttor. Its norm on functions is (integral_0^(2*pi)|h(x)|^2 dx)^(1/2). Source time L^infinity norms and distributional time derivatives use these spatial norms, continuous representatives for suprema and essential suprema for derivative norms, with the same time coordinate as in D004.

inputs.statement: Let 0<sigma_s<=1, tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t in [t_j,t_j+tau_s]. For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. With beta0=2*sigma_s-3/2 for sigma_s<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for sigma_s=1/2 (any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0), and beta0=sigma_s-1 for sigma_s>1/2, the source gives, for beta in [beta0,1+sigma_s], ||Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C*tau_s^((1+sigma_s-beta)/(1+sigma_s-beta0))*||g1||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)*||g2||_(Hsrc^sigma_s), with C depending only on exponents (and epsilon) and uniform in j,tau_s,t and support. Its endpoint formula is (1/6)[S_(-s) Pnz((S_s Dinv g1)(S_s Dinv g2))]_(s=t_j)^(s=t).

argument.text: From D024 and D003, for every real s and periodic distribution h, the squared Hsrc^s norm is 2*pi times the squared H^s norm. Thus finiteness is equivalent, with the identity map on Fourier coefficients. For the completion descriptions, multiplying the norm by the fixed positive scalar sqrt(2*pi) preserves exactly the Cauchy sequences and the equivalence relation of zero-distance sequences of polynomials. Hence the identity on polynomials extends to inverse identity maps of the completions, agreeing as distributions; it preserves zero mean and reality. Consequently ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s), including s=0 and the L2src/L2 identity by D025 and D004. The same identities hold for time suprema and derivative norms because the time variable and distributional derivative are unchanged. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. In E004 set sigma_s=gamma and at gamma=1/2 choose epsilon=1/8. Its a(sigma_s) is exactly agamma. In particular the arbitrary f in H^gamma and g in H^agamma belong to the required source spaces. Substitution of the norm identities and division by sqrt(2*pi) leaves the fixed factor sqrt(2*pi) in the product constant. This proves ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma) for arbitrary f,g in the displayed spaces.

produces.statement: For every real s, Hsrc^s and H^s consist of the same periodic distributions, identified by equal Fourier coefficients, and ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s). At s=0 this identifies L2src with L2; the same constant scales time-supremum norms and norms of distributional time derivatives. Reality and zero mean are preserved.

argument.text: Take arbitrary 0<tau<=1, n>=0 and mean-zero w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. E003 with sigma_s=gamma, g1=g2=w and epsilon=1/8 in the middle case estimates our Stage after the norm conversion proved in S001: w is in Hsrc^gamma, with source norm sqrt(2*pi)||w||_(H^gamma). Both source exponent norms of the stage convert in the same way. Its source integrand equals Bop_s(w,w) by D005 and D016, so the stage is exactly D021, first on polynomials and then by its bounded extension. At beta=agamma the exponent theta=(1+gamma-agamma)/(1+gamma-beta0) equals (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma) for gamma<1/2, 11/17 for gamma=1/2 and (1+gamma)/2 for gamma>1/2. These are >=gamma: in the first case the numerator minus gamma times denominator is gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2>0; the middle is >1/2; the last follows from gamma<=1. In each case beta0<=agamma<=1+gamma and 0<=agamma<1. Since tau<=1, tau^theta<=tau^gamma. At beta=1+gamma the source exponent is zero. This proves both uniform stage estimates, with constants depending only on gamma,M0.

background_notes.justification: Dinv is bounded H^gamma to H^(1+gamma): on nonzero integers, <k>^2/|k|^2<=2. The Airy group preserves every Fourier Sobolev norm and is strongly continuous, by convergence on finitely many modes and uniformly small square-summable tails. For r=1+gamma>1/2, H^r is a multiplication algebra: weighted convolution is bounded in ell^2 using <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r), the ell^1-ell^2 convolution inequality and ||hat h||_ell^1<= (sum <k>^(-2r))^(1/2)||h||_(H^r). The latter series converges for r>1/2. Thus the products in the endpoint formula depend continuously on time in H^r. Pnz is bounded, and the outer Airy group preserves this continuity. Subtracting the fixed initial endpoint gives a continuous stage. The inclusion H^r into H^agamma is bounded because agamma<=r. These facts justify representatives and the routine bounded extension, without resolving the separate epsilon hypothesis.
